- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment turns positive (≥0.36) mid-horizon, model frequently fails to fully capture momentum; increase forecast by 1–4% in the 10–15 day window to align with sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day forecasts when price is >75% above 18-day moving average; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 5–7 days to reflect reversion bias.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.18–0.53), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values to reduce erratic swings.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >2% for 3 consecutive days, model is underestimating upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days to capture trend continuation.
